title: The First Night on the Keepers' Way
fear_reason: Night, a rising wind and the flame shrinking to a blue bead; it turns within the page as the eldest finds the lee of the milestone, and the chapter ends with everyone together, sheltered and falling asleep.

opening_block.last_time: Last time: at every door on the lane the answer was "Not I," until [[child:eldest]] said, "I'll help."

paragraphs.text: Today the flame would leave Candlemere. [[block:ch3.p1.gp]]
[[block:ch3.p2.gp]]
"Please," whispered [[block:ch3.small]].
Everyone waited in a hush, the way you wait for a sneeze…and the flame hopped across. The whole lantern glowed like a jar of honey.
"I wasn't worried at all," said Ember, from behind the log basket. Her ears went flat. *Atchoo!*
[[block:ch3.p5.gp]]
Everyone tried it, even Ember, who was always willing. Nothing happened at all, and she looked terribly pleased.
[[block:ch3.p7.gp]]
[[child:eldest]] read the names, sounding out the hard ones. One was worn so smooth that nobody could read it.
"Whose is that one, worn smooth?" asked [[block:ch3.asker]].
[[block:ch3.p10.gp]]
Ember looked at the smooth name for a long moment, and said nothing at all.
[[block:ch3.p12.gp]]
[[block:ch3.p13]]
[[tierc:jar|default:ch3.jar]]
At sunset the road passed a hollow oak as wide as a doorway. Far ahead stood a shepherd's hut. Then the wind began to rise.
*Whoo*, went the wind. Inside the lantern the flame began to flicker, and shrank and shrank, until it was only a tiny blue bead.
[[child:eldest]]'s heart thumped. Part of [[pro:eldest.obj]] wanted to dash on into the dark. And part of [[pro:eldest.obj]] wanted to run all the way home.
[[cast:Hild]]'s pocket question was still there, like a smooth stone. [[child:eldest]] asked it out loud: "What's the brave thing, and what's the silly thing?"
The wind only blew harder. "Excuse me," said Ember to the wind, very grandly. "That is my tail, and I should like it back."
"Ember, what should we do?" asked [[child:eldest]].
"I know the way home," said Ember gently. "The way on is yours."
[[block:ch3.p21]]
[[child:eldest]] took a lantern breath, the way [[block:ch3.p22.gp]] had shown them, and looked around.
[[block:ch3.p22b]]

It was an old grey milestone, with a little lantern carved on top. [[child:eldest]] read the carving: "West to Wardlow. East to home." The wind roared past one side. On the other, it was almost still.
"The lee," said [[child:eldest]]. That was [[block:ch3.p24.gp]] word for the side of a wall the wind can't reach.
Ember sat down on the still side. "Much better," she said. "My tail agrees."
[[block:ch3.p26]]
[[block:ch3.p28]]
Overhead the stars came out, until the sky was sprinkled like sugar on a dark loaf. Even Ember didn't try to count them.
Inside the lantern the blue bead flickered and bowed, like someone very tired, but it stayed steady.
[[block:ch3.p32.gp]]
[[child:eldest]] wanted to cup the little flame in both hands. But hands go on your knees, never on the lantern: that was [[block:ch3.p27.gp]] rule.
[[block:ch3.p33]]
Ember lifted her nose. "Someone else walked this road tonight," she said. "Someone I know."
"Who?" whispered [[block:ch3.who]].
"Sleep now." The flame was only a blue bead. Would it hold till morning?

classical_echo.source: Odyssey 2: Telemachus slips away by night
classical_echo.grown_up_note: Telemachus steals away at nightfall without telling his mother. These children set out as night comes on too, but with the grandparent's yes, the old law of the road behind them, hugs and a proper goodbye at the gate, and a scarf cast on at home: one row for every night they are away (Penelope's weaving, never commented on).

hook: The flame was only a blue bead. Would it hold till morning?

last_page.what_happened: In the dark and the wind, with a thumping heart, [[child:lead]] stopped to think. Then [[child:lead]] found the lee of the milestone for the little flame.
last_page.calm_close: Fire banked. Sleep low, stay warm, wake bright.

missions.3-4: When someone is getting ready to go out, say "I'll help!" and carry one thing.
missions.5-6: When a grown-up is packing up, be first to say "I'll help," and carry your own things all the way.
missions.7-9: Before you rush at something, ask "What's the brave thing, and what's the silly thing?" Then help with the brave one.

for_the_morning.tell_it_back: At breakfast, ask [[child:eldest]] to tell [[gp:real]] where the little flame spent the night.

vote.setup: The wind is still rising, and the flame is only a blue bead. Where should the heroes carry the lantern, to get it right out of the wind?

options.title: Carry the lantern back to the hollow oak by the road.
options.line: A little way back the way they came, with a trunk as wide as a doorway.

options.title: Go on to the shepherd's hut at the next milestone.
options.line: A little way ahead, with thick stone walls and a low wooden door.

paragraphs.text: All afternoon the Keepers' Way ran west between tall hedges, past stubble fields and a mill-pond and a line of old grey milestones. Ember trotted in front with her tail up like a flag, and stepped round every single puddle. "Wet paws," she said, "are the enemy of a good fox."
The hedges were full of rosehips, as red as Ember's coat. A robin followed them for a whole field, as if it wanted to see where the lantern was going.
[[tierc:favorite|default:ch3.fav.animal]]
Ember bowed to it most politely, but it did not bow back. "No manners at all," she sniffed.
[[child:eldest]] read every milestone out loud, sounding out the old carved letters: how far to the next village, and how far back home. Home was already quite a long way.
[[block:ch3.jar.p5]]
"One, two, three, four, lots," said Ember, helping.
[[tierc:favorite|default:ch3.fav.thing]]
By the time the sun was low and orange, Candlemere was only a smudge of roofs behind them. Nobody talked about it, but everyone looked back once.

tier_c_defaults.text: Once, a brown hare peeked out of the hedge, stared at the lantern, and lolloped off as if it had just remembered a kettle on the boil.
And in the bottom of the backpack, under the apples, rode one small treasure from home: a smooth grey pebble from the cottage path, for luck.

jar_brief.beat: Grandma lights the Keepers' Lantern from her hearth, teaches the lantern breath, and shows her own name on its base. "Whose is that one, worn smooth?" asks Alfie. "That's not mine to tell," says Grandma. She casts on a scarf, and they set out in the afternoon. Night falls on the road, the wind rises, and the flame shrinks to a blue bead. Hugh sets the lantern down in the lee of a milestone, and he and Alfie kneel round it with their backs to the wind, hands on their knees, not on the lantern. Clara is already asleep in Ember's tail. Ember lifts her nose: "Someone else walked this road tonight. Someone I know." "Who?" "Sleep now."

flags_for_jon: The paywall ending (canon §8, used word for word) is split into four paragraphs so each has one speaker, as kit 1d allows. The last paragraph is then "Sleep now." The flame was only a blue bead. Would it hold till morning?", and the picture of everyone together (the lantern in the lee, the wall of backs, the youngest asleep in Ember's tail) sits two paragraphs before. Suggest the checker reads the canon's closing lines as one unit.

Two canon wordings for the same moment: the chapter table says they kneel round the lantern "hands on their knees, not on the lantern"; the paywall text says they "made a wall with their backs to the wind". Both are kept: the hands rule comes just before the paywall paragraph, as the grandparent's rule, and the paywall words describe the wall.

Lighting the lantern (fire canon). The grandparent opens the little door and holds the lantern close to the hearth; nobody holds a taper or an open flame. The grandparent says the world's rule ("Fire won't be taken. It has to be given, and somebody has to ask."), the youngest asks ("Please"), and the flame hops across by itself through the chimney, then stands up, stretches and looks about. Ember's first fib-sneeze follows ("I wasn't worried at all"). New lines inside the beat; no canon change.

Part 1's jar slot ("onboarding details") is a reviewed side scene on the afternoon road (ch3.jar, 150 to 250 words) holding two favorites slots with reviewed defaults: a favorite animal peeking out (ch3.fav.animal, a hare) and a small treasure in the backpack (ch3.fav.thing), as canon §3 describes. Ember's reaction after the animal ("Ember had bowed to it most politely, and nobody had bowed back. 'No manners at all.'") is written to fit any animal a family's favorite puts there. Prompt 2 takes one FAVORITE_SLOT a night, so either it fills both, or code picks one and the other runs its default.

The Pause & ask comes straight after the eldest asks the pocket question, before Ember's "The way on is yours", and its question is about that stop ("Why do you think Hugh stopped to ask a question, instead of dashing on in the dark?"), so every prompt can be answered at that point: the youngest is asked the flame's color (blue). It stays inside 35% to 65% with any jar scene (59% with 150 words, 63% with 250).

The youngest's act at the crisis: in the dark, the youngest spots the milestone ("Big stone!"), and that is where the eldest finds the lee. One child: Ember points her nose at it (no sibling is invented).

Vote 1 is set up in the story: just before sunset they pass a hollow oak by the road, and a shepherd's hut stands far ahead by the next milestone. The milestone they shelter by has a little lantern carved on its top (canon §2, every seventh milestone), a quiet seed for Hild's Chapter 35 clue.

New details inside the beat, no canon change: the youngest's "Please" as the flame is given; the milestone carving "West to Wardlow. East to home." (the eldest's line); Ember to the wind, "That is my tail, and I should like it back."; the middle child's "I'll help. Lantern up!" in the dark; the youngest's "Night night, little flame"; the stars; the grandparent knitting the first row of the scarf far behind them; "And this fire stays awake till you're home."

The grandparent says yes by naming the old law of the Keepers' Way (any child carrying the lantern is fed and housed at every door), and there are hugs and a proper goodbye at the gate. That reverses Telemachus slipping away unseen. The scarf is cast on at home, one row a night.

Ember and the choice: asked what to do, Ember answers only "I know the way home. The way on is yours.", and the eldest says the brave thing out loud himself ("The silly thing is running on in the dark. The brave thing is stopping here, and keeping the flame out of the wind."). No narrator states it.
Vote 1 copy: the canon's two options as titles, with a calm line each. Neither route needs an access version (bible §6 lists only votes 5, 6 and 11).
Rich words: steady and lee (new), with flicker (Part 1's week word), hush and willing brought back from Chapters 1 and 2. steady and lee are left to come back in Chapters 4 and 5.

Tool notes: check-chapter.py scores the whole jar default as one paragraph when it looks for speakers, so the default keeps Ember as its only tagged speaker ("hummed", not "sang"). It can't match the apostrophe in "Keepers'" as a place name, so the source lists "Keepers'" in allowed_names (all three drafts did this). The picture-book jar pictures name no animal, so they fit whatever favorite a family's jar scene shows.
